sentences: In a field under a high blue sky stand two figures.
A half-clothed woman holding a basket turns her head to look straight at us, and beside her is a girl with bobbed hair.
The canvas is more than 1.
6 metres wide.
The painter, Yi In-seong, came from the city of Daegu.
He was first accepted into the Joseon Art Exhibition at seventeen, and with this painting, made at twenty-two, he won a special prize at its 13th edition in 1934.
Begin with the sky above.
White clouds drift across deep blue, making the autumn sky feel especially high and deep.
This wide blue sky fills nearly half of the whole picture.
Let's move closer to the woman's face.
Her backward glance meets ours directly, and it is striking.
Her reddish-brown skin and rather stiff pose recall the Tahitian women painted by Gauguin.
Now look at the girl beside her, with her bobbed hair and sleeveless dress.
The two are in fact the painter's own younger sisters.
He based them on a photograph taken in Daegu in August 1933.
Look at the basket tucked against the woman's side.
The same basket appears in his still life Roses from that year.
The wrapping cloth beside it, too, was a prop he kept hanging in his studio and painted again and again.
To the upper right, drooping sunflowers bow their heads, while corn, reeds and grasses turn yellow.
The clothes say midsummer but the landscape says autumn, because he painted the scenery separately that autumn.
That mismatch is part of its charm.
Now come down to the red earth below.
Red ground clashes boldly with blue sky, adding heat to the whole scene.
Yi reportedly set out to paint Korea's deep blue autumn sky and red soil as symbols of the land.
The bold primary colours and decorative layout borrow from Gauguin.
Yet Yi tried to capture Korean feeling through Korean faces and familiar fields.
It is often called the fullest expression of the Korean local colour debated in the 1930s.
Some critics, though, fault it for picturing colonial Korea as a fragile woman and child.
Opinions also divide on whether it catered to the official judges' taste or voiced national feeling.
The very next year, Yi went on to take the exhibition's top prize, the Changdeokgung Prize.
He died in 1950, only thirty-eight.
Step back once more and feel the gap between summer clothes and the autumn field.
Why do you think the woman has turned to look back at us?
